problem: Embodied simulators assume deaf agents in silent environments. The audio-capable ones are limited: SoundSpaces uses pre-computed impulse responses on a discrete grid at a fixed height, and ThreeDWorld uses box-shaped room approximations. No prior audio-visual navigation policy had been shown to transfer sim-to-real.
motivation: Household robots need to hear, localize sounds and follow voice commands, so realistic continuous audio rendering with human-in-the-loop VR is needed. Semantic audio-visual navigation is hard because sounds are short and the agent must localize the source after it stops. The authors observe that navigation features and occupancy anticipation should benefit each other.
key_idea: Build Sonicverse, a real-time continuous multisensory simulator (iGibson 2.0 plus Resonance Audio with full scene geometry and materials, and a VR audio interface), and train a multi-task agent that jointly predicts actions and occupancy maps, with successful sim2real transfer.
insight: Jointly learning occupancy anticipation regularizes the audio-visual state features, and this improves semantic audio-visual navigation over SAVi on all metrics for both heard and unheard sounds. Sim2real needs three fixes: mixing recorded robot ego-noise into the training audio, randomizing source gain, and calibrating depth range (0.8-3.5 m) to match simulation. No separate ablation of the occupancy head is reported; the evidence is the comparison to SAVi, which shares the base architecture.
method: Acoustic simulation: Resonance Audio renders direct sound with distance attenuation and near-field effects, ray-count-based dynamic occlusion with frequency-dependent filtering, and binaural HRTF output.

Reverb baking: reverb probes are spread through the scene, and the closest probe supplies pre-computed RT60s. Early reflections are rendered on the fly with a box approximation relative to the probe. Mesh semantic categories are mapped to acoustic material types.
Environments: 85 Matterport3D scenes (517 m² average) and 15 interactive iGibson scenes; sounds can be attached to objects, including moving ones, or to rooms.
Audio-visual VR interface: streams a human's voice through OpenVR headsets to the agent, enabling speaker following, voice-driven object retrieval and auditory orientation training.
Navigation model: SAVi-style goal predictor plus audio-visual scene-memory transformer feeding an actor-critic, trained in two stages with DD-PPO, using continuous wheel-velocity actions.

Occupancy head: a U-Net predicts the 5m x 5m egocentric occupancy map from the depth-projected local map, with the tiled state feature s_t fused into the last three encoder layers, trained with BCE jointly with navigation.
Sim2Real: a TurtleBot with a binaural mic and RGB-D camera, GMapping pose replacing GPS, ego-noise mixing, gain randomization and depth calibration.

setting.backbone: SAVi-style scene memory transformer + actor-critic with U-Net occupancy head (trained from scratch, DD-PPO)
setting.training_data: Simulated semantic audio-visual navigation episodes in Sonicverse on iGibson and Matterport3D scenes with 15 semantic sounds; no external data (recorded robot ego-noise used for augmentation in sim2real)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth + binaural audio spectrogram + bump sensor + pose relative to start
setting.simulator: Sonicverse (iGibson 2.0 + Resonance Audio), Matterport3D and iGibson scenes
setting.privileged: none at test time (occupancy ground truth from meshes used only as training supervision; real-world pose from GMapping SLAM, GPS pointer for AudioPointGoal)

numbers_note: The paper's own benchmark is new (Sonicverse semantic audio-visual navigation with continuous actions), so all benchmarks are tagged 'other'. Split naming is 'test' (unseen environments); the paper does not use official split names.
results: On the Sonicverse benchmark the multi-task model beats SAVi on all metrics, e.g. iGibson heard SR 60.2 vs 53.0 and Matterport3D heard SR 38.4 vs 27.9, and it far outperforms Gan et al. and Chen et al. In sim2real on a real TurtleBot, AudioGoal reaches 30% SR and AudioPointGoal 50% SR over 10 trials.
limitations: Sim2Real evaluation is small (10 trials, one bedroom) and relies on SLAM pose and audio/depth augmentation.
Early reflections use a box-shaped approximation and reverb is baked on static geometry only, and object impact sounds are not modeled.
No ablation isolating the occupancy head; the gain is inferred from comparison with SAVi.
compares_to: Gan et al. (Look, Listen, and Act)
